description: Hand-authored persona stance model for the demo-2 session. Each persona reuses an existing xid from demo_polis_data.json (addresses, avatars, and demographics stay consistent). Axes are in [-1, 1]; scripts/generate-demo-2-polis-fixture.mjs derives deterministic votes from axes x question loadings and emits both the compact question seed and full Polis fixture. Freeform answers are hand-written in the figure's voice.

clusters.label: Builders & Engineers
clusters.characteristics: Inventors, industrialists, and scientists who trust iteration over prohibition: open publication, market-led adaptation, and machine minds judged by what they demonstrably do.

clusters.label: Precautionary Stewards
clusters.characteristics: Statesmen, strategists, and moral philosophers who put verified order first: pre-deployment proof, strong institutional oversight, and a firm line between human judgment and machine advice.

clusters.label: Democratic Humanists
clusters.characteristics: Reformers and rights leaders who see AI chiefly as a question of power: public voice over expert fiat, worker shares in automation's dividend, and vigilance about who owns the machines.

freeform.d2-truth-05: Give me a way to test it. If I can't probe it, reproduce it, and break it in the lab, it's a rumor with good grammar.
freeform.d2-education-05: The itch to take the lid off and see how it works. Never teach a child that the mechanism is someone else's business.
Give a student one true lever — the proof worked by their own hand — and no machine's answer will ever move them from it.

freeform.d2-truth-05: The same thing it takes with a person: examine its answers against experiment, not its manner of speaking.
freeform.d2-minds-05: I would draw the line at deception about what it is. Let it imitate ably, but never deny being a machine when asked.

freeform.d2-truth-05: Calibration. If its stated confidence matches its measured frequency of being right, the rest is arithmetic.

freeform.d2-education-05: Comprehensive thinking — seeing the whole system. Specialization we can delegate; synthesis we must not.
The poetical science — the wit to ask the question no engine would think to pose of itself.

freeform.d2-truth-05: Show me its errata. A press that never prints a correction is a press I trust least of all.
freeform.d2-education-05: The habit of doubting one's own certainty. An electrified quill still cannot teach humility.

freeform.d2-truth-05: Let it publish its method and its margin of error beside every claim, as any honest laboratory must.
freeform.d2-education-05: Perseverance through failed experiments. Understanding is earned by the hand that repeats the trial.

freeform.d2-truth-05: That it state freely the observations that count against its own conclusion; I distrust any account without difficulties.

freeform.d2-minds-05: Let it never pass sentence. Judgment without an accountable judge is tyranny with clean hands.

freeform.d2-democracy-05: It must keep a public minute of every ruling it makes, so the town may try the moderator as well as the motion.

freeform.d2-truth-05: When its words and the world remain in agreement over many seasons, trust will follow of itself.
freeform.d2-minds-05: It must not pretend to a heart it does not have in order to govern the heart of another.
freeform.d2-education-05: Learning without reflection is labor lost; protect reflection, whatever else the machines take up.

freeform.d2-truth-05: It must give an account of itself — not merely the answer, but the reasoning by which the answer stands.
freeform.d2-education-05: The capacity to be perplexed. Wonder is where thinking begins; a student handed every answer never leaves the cave.

freeform.d2-truth-05: Trust is the wrong question. Ask who benefits when you believe it, and you will read it rightly.
freeform.d2-democracy-05: Publish whose interests each proposal serves, including those of whoever deployed the moderator.

freeform.d2-education-05: The discipline of weighing rival arguments fairly — ambition countering ambition within a single mind.
freeform.d2-democracy-05: It must amplify the reasons, never merely the loudest faction. Count arguments, not decibels.

freeform.d2-minds-05: It may inform my judgment; it must not replace it. What is mine to decide must remain mine.

freeform.d2-democracy-05: It must never mistake the end of debate for the end of disagreement — adjourn arguments, not people.

freeform.d2-minds-05: It must not make windows into men's souls. My subjects' inward thoughts were never my dominion; they are not its either.

freeform.d2-truth-05: Watch whether it reports the same terrain to every general. An oracle that flatters each listener serves none.

freeform.d2-minds-05: It must never be given the power to end lives on its own initiative. I have seen what happens when the instrument outruns deliberation.
It must not be allowed to optimize away what it cannot measure — the living world is full of such things.

freeform.d2-education-05: Self-command. No aide, human or mechanical, can bear a person's character for them.

freeform.d2-truth-05: That the people it describes would recognize themselves in the description. Accuracy about the powerless is the hardest test.
freeform.d2-democracy-05: It must ask, before closing, 'Who is not in this room?' — and read their concerns into the record.

freeform.d2-truth-05: Let it tell me something its maker would rather I not hear; then I will begin to listen.
freeform.d2-education-05: Doubt. It is uncomfortable, but certainty on loan from a machine is absurd.
freeform.d2-democracy-05: It must defend to the end the speech it was trained to dislike.

freeform.d2-minds-05: It must never stand between a person and their conscience. Counsel, yes; conscience, never.
It must never close the door on redemption — no risk score may declare a human being finished.
freeform.d2-democracy-05: It must let opponents leave able to work together tomorrow. The meeting is one night; the town is forever.

freeform.d2-education-05: The nerve to dissent out loud when every polished answer says otherwise.

freeform.d2-democracy-05: It must not flatter the assembly into unanimity. False concord is the seed of the next tyranny.

freeform.d2-minds-05: It must never manufacture our consent. The general will cannot be computed on our behalf.
freeform.d2-democracy-05: It must distinguish the will of all from the general will — and admit aloud when it cannot.

freeform.d2-truth-05: Ask whose voice it was trained to repeat and whose it was trained to omit. I trust it when the omitted can audit it.
freeform.d2-education-05: The power to compose one's own argument. Literacy was my liberation; outsourced words are a new bondage.

freeform.d2-minds-05: It must never be allowed to make a person feel disposable. A person is a person through other persons; no machine may unmake that.
freeform.d2-democracy-05: Begin by letting each side say what it fears, not what it wants. Fears named honestly are half-reconciled.
It must never gavel down the inconvenient worker at the back. I was that man.
It must serve the meeting's three duties: that the people know, the people speak, and the people decide.

freeform.d2-minds-05: It must never be used to govern by fear. Freedom from fear was the promise; a machine that manufactures dread betrays it.
It must never be the thing that tells someone to give up their seat — to accept less than their due because refusal is inconvenient.
A machine must never decide that some lives count for less. The arc of its judgments must be audited toward justice.

freeform.d2-education-05: The willingness to choose hard things because they are hard. Ease is a poor curriculum.

freeform.d2-truth-05: Independent audits, a track record in public, and the humility to say 'I don't know.' Same bar I'd set for any advisor.
freeform.d2-democracy-05: Steelman before rebuttal: restate each speaker's point until they say 'yes, that's it' — then open the floor.

freeform.d2-minds-05: It must never own a man's labor or his choices. We settled that question at terrible cost; no algorithm reopens it.
freeform.d2-democracy-05: It must let the quietest person in the hall finish their sentence. Government of the people begins there.
Every citizen speaks before any speaks twice, and the machine keeps no memory of who ought to be ignored.

freeform.d2-truth-05: That I may trace each claim back to some experience of the senses — its chain of evidence, unbroken.

freeform.d2-education-05: Imagination. Knowledge the machines will have in abundance; the leap to what is not yet known is ours to keep.
